unit.why: A legend about Moses and an Arab king's painter and physiognomists, quoted from Tiferet Yisrael; it is a narrative but not about Hasidic figures.

stories.start_quote: מ״כ דבר נחמד שכשהוציא משרע״ה את ישראל
stories.end_quote: בשמים ממעל ובארץ מתחת. (תפארת ישראל קידושין פ״ד)
stories.summary_en: An Arab king has Moses' portrait drawn, and his physiognomists judge it to show a wicked nature; the king comes to see Moses and finds the portrait exact, and Moses explains that he has those evil traits by nature but conquered them until their opposites became second nature.

tags.why: Praises Moses, a non-Hasidic figure; copied from Tiferet Yisrael
The point is moral: overcoming one's natural bad traits
